The three component choices are permitted by Countable Choice, and $v=(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ then satisfies $\|u-v\|_{L^2(d^3\mathbf k)}<\varepsilon/3$.

For each $m$, [F5] supplies a smooth cutoff $\rho_m$ equal to $1$ on $\overline B_{1/m}(0)$ and supported in $B_{2/m}(0)$; set $\chi_m=1-\rho_m$. By [F3], $\lambda_3(B_{2/m}(0))=4\pi\int_0^{2/m}r^2\,dr=(4\pi/3)(2/m)^3$. Since $v$ is bounded,

The operators $P_\sigma$ are self-adjoint and
$$P_\sigma^2=\frac{P+2\sigma h+h^2}{4}=P_\sigma,\qquad P_+P_-=0,\qquad P_++P_-=P.$$

Continuity makes $P_\sigma(\mathbf n)v$ nonzero on a neighborhood of $\mathbf n_0$, and normalizing this smooth vector gives a smooth unit local section. Set $g_m(\mathbf k)=P(\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|)\chi_m(\mathbf k)v(\mathbf k)$. It is smooth, transverse, and compactly supported away from $0$. Since $Pu=u$ for the transverse field $u$ and $\|P(\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|)\|\le1$ by step 1.1,

derivations.claim:
The vectors $\mathbf e_\theta,\mathbf e_\varphi$ are real unit vectors orthogonal to each other and to $\mathbf n$, and $\mathbf n\times\mathbf e_\theta=\mathbf e_\varphi$, $\mathbf n\times\mathbf e_\varphi=-\mathbf e_\theta$. Hence $e_\sigma$ has unit norm and satisfies $h(\mathbf n)e_\sigma=\sigma e_\sigma$, so it is a local frame of $\mathcal L_{\sigma,\mathbf n}$. Direct differentiation gives $\mathbf e_\theta\cdot d\mathbf e_\varphi=-\cos\theta\,d\varphi$ and $\mathbf e_\varphi\cdot d\mathbf e_\theta=\cos\theta\,d\varphi$; the diagonal terms vanish. Therefore
$$e_\sigma^\dagger de_\sigma=\frac{i\sigma}{2}(\mathbf e_\theta\cdot d\mathbf e_\varphi-\mathbf e_\varphi\cdot d\mathbf e_\theta)=-i\sigma\cos\theta\,d\varphi.$$
Multiplying by $-i$ gives $A_\sigma=-\sigma\cos\theta\,d\varphi$, and differentiating gives $F_\sigma=\sigma\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\varphi$.

The phase factors defining $e_\sigma^N$ and $e_\sigma^S$ cancel the azimuthal singularities at the north and south poles, respectively. For example, near the north pole $(1-\cos\theta)e^{2i\varphi}=(n_1+in_2)^2/(1+\cos\theta)$ and $\sin\theta e^{i\varphi}=n_1+in_2$, which are smooth there; the south-pole formulas use $(1+\cos\theta)e^{-2i\varphi}=(n_1-in_2)^2/(1-\cos\theta)$ and $\sin\theta e^{-i\varphi}=n_1-in_2$. Thus these are smooth unit gauges on northern and southern neighborhoods. On their overlap, $e_\sigma^N=e^{2i\sigma\varphi}e_\sigma^S$, whose transition map winds $2\sigma$ times as $\varphi$ traverses the equator once.

Since $F_\sigma=\sigma d\Omega$, [F2] gives $\int_{S^2}F_\sigma=4\pi\sigma$, hence the normalized Berry flux is $2\sigma$. The skew-Hermitian curvature is $\Omega_\sigma=d\omega_\sigma=iF_\sigma$ because $\omega_\sigma=iA_\sigma$. Under the stated Chern-Weil convention,
$$c_1(\mathcal L_\sigma)[S^2]=\frac{i}{2\pi}\int_{S^2}iF_\sigma=-\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^2}F_\sigma=-2\sigma.$$

Suppose a global smooth unit section $s$ of $\mathcal L_\sigma$ existed. Then $A_s=-i\,s^\dagger ds$ would be a globally defined smooth real one-form. On each local unit frame, writing $s=g e_\sigma$ with $|g|=1$ gives $A_s=A_\sigma-i g^{-1}dg$; the correction is closed because $d(g^{-1}dg)=-g^{-2}dg\wedge dg=0$, so $dA_s=F_\sigma$. The sphere is compact, oriented, and boundaryless, so [F3] yields $\int_{S^2}F_\sigma=\int_{S^2}dA_s=\int_{\partial S^2}A_s=0$. This contradicts $\int_{S^2}F_\sigma=4\pi\sigma\ne0$ from step 2.1. Therefore no global smooth unit helicity eigenvector exists.
